name: Is keeping the same bathroom layout always the cheapest option?

mainEntity.name: Is keeping the same bathroom layout always the cheapest option?

acceptedAnswer.text: Keeping fixtures in their current locations can be a sensible budget strategy, but it should not be treated as automatically inexpensive. The project may still involve demolition, waterproofing, electrical changes, ventilation, subfloor repairs, cabinetry, tile, and inspection work. It can also preserve an inefficient arrangement if the real problem is circulation or storage. Ask for a same-location design and a reconfigured design with clearly separated scopes. Elite Remodeling & Design can use the comparison to show what added function each layout change provides.
acceptedAnswer.description: Usually, keeping plumbing near its current locations reduces some rough-in work, but total cost still depends on demolition, waterproofing, electrical, ventilation, cabinetry, tile, hidden damage, and inspections. Compare a same-location plan with a reconfigured plan so savings are weighed against lost function.
